 DISTRICT JUDGE AND ADDL. MACT, BELAGAVI IN MVC  NO.1961/2017 AND GRANT THE COMPENSATION AS PRAYED BY THE  APPELLANT, HEREIN IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
 JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11550-DB  MFA No. 102968 of 2022 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KRISHNA S.DIXIT  AND  THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL
ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL)

This appeal by the injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 8.7.2022 passed in MVC No.1961/2017 on the file of learned XI Addl. District Judge & Addl. MACT, Belagavi1.
2.

Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, the claimant/injured filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the accidental injuries sustained on 17.11.2016 involving Royal Enfield Bullet bearing registration No.MH-50/E-3309 and Bus bearing registration No.MH-09/CV- 7890.
Due to the accident, he has suffered permanent physical disability.
The claimant was aged about 32 years at the time of the accident, was doing mason work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
3. On appearance, respondent No.2/Insurance Company has filed statement of objections denying the claim petition averments.

It was contended that the accident 'Tribunal', for short NC:
2024:KHC-D:11550-DB occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motorcycle in question.
Thus, sought dismissal of the claim petition.

4. The Tribunal on scrutiny of entire material available on record allowed the claim petition in part awarding a total compensation of Rs.2,47,136/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Aggrieved by the same, the claimant/injured is in appeal.

5. Learned counsel Sri. Umesh C Ainapur appearing for the appellant/injured vehemently contends that the Tribunal has erred in assessing disability of the claimant at 10% to the whole body, which is on the lower side and contrary to the oral testimony of PW2-Doctor and other medical evidence on record.

He also submits that the award of compensation under other heads is also on the lower side,
hence, seeks enhancement of the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Preeti Shashank appearing for the respondent/Insurer supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that PW2 is a stalk doctor and there is only one fracture i.e. fracture of tibia and fibula, hence, the Tribunal is justified in assessing disability NC: 2024:KHC-D:11550-DB of the injured at 10%, which does not call for interference.
She further submits that taking note of pleadings and evidence, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under all other heads, which needs no interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, she seeks dismissal of appeal.
7. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.
8. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 17.11.2016, the appellant sustained fracture of tibia and fibula.
In support of the claim, the claimant examined the doctor as PW2, who deposed that the claimant has suffered fracture of tibia and fibula.
He further deposed that the claimant has got permanent physical disability to an extent of 42% to left lower limb and 18% to the right lower limb.

The evidence of PW2 cannot be believed with regard to disability, however, taking note of the injuries suffered by the claimant and considering the treatment provided and also duration of treatment taken by him, this Court is of the considered opinion that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability of the claimant at 15% to the whole body instead of 10% assessed by the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11550-DB Tribunal.
There is no dispute with regard to income of the injured at Rs.8,750/- per month assessed by the Tribunal, age of the injured as 32 years and appropriate multiplier of 16.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of future earnings due to disability as under:
Rs.8,750 x 12 x 16 x 15/100 = Rs.2,52,000/-
9.
The medical evidence on record indicates that the appellant was an inpatient for a period of three months.

Taking note of the same, we are of the considered view that the compensation awarded under other heads is on the lower side, which requires to be re-assessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 40,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 4,136/-
 Loss of future earning Rs.2,52,000/-

Food, transport & attendant charges Rs. 30,000/-
 Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 25,000/-
 ----------------
 Total Rs.3,81,136/-
 ----------------
 10.

In all, the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,81,136/- as against Rs.2,47,136/-

3 awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
11. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal stands partly allowed.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11550-DB b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,81,136/- as against Rs.2,47,136/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The respondent/insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.
f) TCR be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.

g) Draw modified award accordingly.
h) No order as to costs.
Sd/-
(KRISHNA S.DIXIT) JUDGE Sd/-
